# synology-dsm Provider

Provider for managing Synology DSM packages, Container Manager projects, files in shared folders, TLS certificates, reverse proxy entries, firewall rules, Task Scheduler tasks, system settings, users, groups, shared folders, permissions, quotas, and user home service.

The provider uses the Synology DSM web API and is developed against DSM 7.2.2
and DSM 7.3.2. DSM 6.x and model-specific packages may behave differently.

The public Registry source is `batonogov/synology-dsm`; the preferred local name
and resource prefix remain `dsm`.

## Authentication

Configure `host`, `username`, and `password` in HCL or with the
`SYNOLOGY_DSM_HOST`, `SYNOLOGY_DSM_USERNAME`, and `SYNOLOGY_DSM_PASSWORD`
environment variables. Explicit HCL values take precedence. Use `insecure` only
when connecting to a trusted DSM with a self-signed TLS certificate.

Terraform sensitive values are redacted in normal output but are not encrypted
inside state. Protect state files and backups accordingly.

## Task execution is remote code execution

The `dsm_scheduled_task` and `dsm_event_task` resources create entries in DSM
Task Scheduler. Those entries run a shell command on the NAS, and DSM runs them
as the account you name — in practice `root`, because that is what the tasks
people automate need.

That makes these two resource types different in kind from the rest of this
provider. Everywhere else, write access to the Terraform configuration grants
control over DSM objects. Here it grants **arbitrary code execution as `root` on
the NAS**: whoever can edit the configuration, approve a pull request that
touches it, or supply a variable that reaches `command`, can run anything on the
NAS with full privileges — including reading every share and disabling the very
audit trail that would show it happened.

Treat this as the privilege boundary it is:

- Both resources are disabled by default. Set `allow_task_execution = true` (or
  `SYNOLOGY_DSM_ALLOW_TASK_EXECUTION=true`) only in workspaces that need them.
  A configuration that leaves the flag off fails at plan time, so a team can
  keep the capability switched off outright.
- `command` is deliberately **not** marked sensitive. Hiding a root command from
  `terraform plan` output would remove the one place a reviewer can see what is
  about to be installed on the NAS. Review plan diffs for these resources the
  way you review a change to CI configuration.
- Prefer literal commands over interpolated ones. A `command` built from a
  variable or a remote data source moves the privilege boundary to whoever
  controls that input.
- Restrict who may run Terraform against DSM at all: the provider needs a DSM
  administrator account, and task creation cannot be delegated more narrowly.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    dsm = {
      source  = "batonogov/synology-dsm"
      version = "0.1.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "dsm" {
  host     = "https://diskstation:5001"
  username = "admin"
  password = var.dsm_password
  insecure = true

  # dsm_scheduled_task and dsm_event_task run shell commands on the NAS as root.
  # They are refused at plan time unless this is enabled, so that write access to
  # this configuration does not silently mean root on the NAS.
  # allow_task_execution = true
}

variable "dsm_password" {
  description = "DSM administrator password"
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) Synology DSM URL (e.g. https://diskstation:5001)
- `password` (String, Sensitive) DSM administrator password
- `username` (String) DSM administrator username

### Optional

- `allow_task_execution` (Boolean) Allow the `dsm_scheduled_task` and `dsm_event_task` resources. **These resources run arbitrary commands on the NAS, normally as `root`. Anyone who can change this Terraform configuration — or open a pull request against it — can execute code as `root` on the NAS.** Defaults to `false`, which makes both resource types fail at plan time so a team can keep them disabled outright. May also be set with `SYNOLOGY_DSM_ALLOW_TASK_EXECUTION=true`. Data sources are never gated: reading existing tasks executes nothing.
- `insecure` (Boolean) Skip TLS certificate verification (for self-signed certs)
- `timeout` (String) Timeout for ordinary DSM requests, as a Go duration such as `60s` or `2m`. Defaults to `30s`. Raise it for slower hardware or a NAS under load. Lifecycle operations that block while DSM works — creating a Container Manager project, writing a compose file — always get at least five minutes regardless of this value, because their duration is bounded by the NAS rather than by the network.
